To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a paramagnetic silver cluster consisting of six silver nuclei was prepared by aqueous cation exchange in an LTA type zeolite.
the Ag(6) cluster reacts with NO to form an Ag(5)NO complex.
the silver clusters react with NO at room temperature and that the NO(2) molecules exhibit dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reaction of adsorbed nitrogen oxides with silver clusters supported on zeolite.
the reactivity of NO on a well-defined silver cluster.
the characterization of silver containing zeolites and the reaction of NO with the Ag(6) cluster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO molecule is bound to a single silver atom, and that the NO(2) is bound to the Ag(6) cluster.
NO(2) is formed from adsorbed NO at 300 K, but that the reaction is slow.
the Ag(6) cluster is an active catalyst for the reaction of NO with NO to NO(2) at room temperature, and that NO(2) is adsorbed on the silver cluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ag(6)(NO(2)) is a model system for the study of the reaction of NO with silver containing catalysts, and the rotational motion is an important factor for the catalytic activity.
the Ag(6) cluster is an efficient catalyst for the reaction of NO with NO(2) to form N(2)O(3), and the reaction proceeds with a turnover frequency of 0.3 s(-1).
the NO molecule is strongly bound to the silver cluster, and the adsorbed nitrite is mobile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EPR technique is a powerful tool to characterize adsorbed molecules at low temperature.
the silver clusters are very reactive and can be oxidized and reduced by NO.
silver cluster catalysts can be used to oxidize NO into NO(2).
